note: Jordan Love is the QB12 in fantasy points per game. It was nice to see that in Josh Jacobs' first game back, Green Bay didn't dial back their passing rate. In Weeks 1-6, Green Bay had a 65.9% pass rate, and last week they actually bumped it a tad higher to 70.8%. Overall, they have the second-best passing rate in the NFL. Among 34 qualifying passers, Love has still struggled with accuracy, ranking 22nd in passing success rate and 28th in catchable target rate, but he is also tenth in hero throw rate and 14th in passing touchdown rate. This week, Love will have a tougher matchup. Since Week 4, Carolina has continued to field a strong pass defense, allowing the 11th-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 13th-lowest passing success rate. Love has the volume, the talent, and the skilled receivers to overcome a strong pass defense.

Matthew Stafford is the QB15 in fantasy points per game, as it has been a roller coaster ride some weeks with Stafford. He has three games with at least 22.9 fantasy points while also logging three outings with less than 17 fantasy points. Among 34 qualifying passers, Stafford is 17th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, and 19th in catchable target rate. Stafford could post another QB1 week against the Bolts. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the 15th-lowest passing success rate, and ranked 16th in passing touchdown rate allowed. It's a middle-of-the-road matchup for Stafford.

Jacoby Brissett is the QB22 in fantasy points per game with two outings this season with at least 25 fantasy points. Among 34 qualifying passers, Brissett is 32nd in yards per attempt, 18th in passing success rate, tenth in highly accurate throw rate, and 14th in catchable target rate. Brissett could return to the friendly confines of QB1 land this week. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-highest CPOE, and the sixth-most EPA per dropback.

Caleb Williams is the QB6 in fantasy points per game. Since returning from his hamstring injury, Williams has averaged only 10.5 rushing yards, so I don't see that being a huge part of his game this week. If his hamstring is back to 100%, maybe he surprises me, though. Among 34 qualifying passers, Williams is fifth in yards per attempt, fifth in passing success rate, second in highly accurate throw rate, and first in catchable target rate. He is having a wonderful season as he has improved his accuracy. This will be a huge test for how much he has grown this week. Seattle's pass defense is a buzz saw. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the tenth-lowest CPOE, and the third-lowest EPA per dropback. In most leagues, despite the horrible matchup, you're still starting Williams.

Jared Goff has been crushing it this season as the QB3 in fantasy points per game. Among 34 qualifying passers, Goff is eighth in yards per attempt, fourth in passing touchdown rate and passing success rate, third in hero throw rate, and sixth in catchable target rate. Goff will have to deal with a Minnesota pass defense that has been easily the best pass defense in the NFL. Ok, fine, Seattle is also in that convo, but Minny has been amazing. Over the last five games, Minny has allowed the fewest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, and the lowest passing touchdown rate. Overall, Minnesota has created havoc weekly, leading the NFL in blitz rate and pressure rate. Goff has navigated the blitz well this season, but he will have to be elite in this regard this week. Among 29 qualifying passers, Goff has been quite good against the blitz, ranking sixth in yards per attempt and third in passing success rate. Goff could get it done this week, but there's a sizable range of outcomes for him this week.

Even after last week's stinker, Bryce Young is the QB8 in fantasy points per game. Last week, Young completed only 51.8% of his passes with 163 passing yards (6.4 yards per attempt), a 69.6% catchable throw rate, and two picks. Overall, Young (among 34 qualifying passers) is 13th in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, 26th in catchable throw rate, and 12th in hero throw rate. If Young is going to bounce back this week, he'll have to do so against a solid Green Bay pass defense. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the seventh-lowest CPOE. Green Bay during that stretch also has had the 12th-lowest pressure rate, so Young should have clean pockets this week. It's a good litmus test matchup to see if Young has turned back into a pumpkin prior to Halloween.

Kyler Murray has been a disaster at quarterback this season as the QB34 in fantasy points per game. He has run more in his last two games, averaging 7.5 attempts and 45 yards on the ground, but in the passing department he has been wretched. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 23rd in yards per attempt, 31st in passing success rate, 28th in aDOT, and dead last in highly accurate throw rate. Murray could have a nice game this week, but I don't have any faith in him to take advantage of a nice matchup. Across their last five games, Detroit has allowed the fifth-highest passing touchdown rate, the third-highest passing success rate, the fourth-highest passer rating, and the ninth-highest CPOE. Detroit in that span also has the fourth-best pressure rate and has ranked 12th in quick pressure rate. If Detroit's pass rush can rattle Murray this week, it could be his undoing.

Patrick Mahomes II has been slumping. As the QB17 in fantasy points per game, he hasn't had more than 17 fantasy points in any game since Week 2. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is tenth in yards per attempt, sixth in passing success rate, 18th in passing touchdown rate, and 23rd in highly accurate throw rate. Mahomes hasn't thrown for a touchdown since Week 4. I don't see this week as the matchup where Mahomes turns it around. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the ninth-lowest passing success rate, and the third-lowest fantasy points per dropback.

Kirk Cousins is the QB11 in fantasy points per game as he leads the NFL in passing touchdowns (16). Among 34 qualifying passers, he is third in passing yards, 14th in yards per attempt, 22nd in highly accurate throw rate, 27th in catchable target rate, and 22nd in hero throw rate. Cousins should have another QB1 outing this week. Across their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 13th-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing touchdown rate, the fifth-highest passing success rate, and the seventh-most EPA per dropback.

Sam Darnold has been a ghost for most of the season as the QB27 in fantasy points per game. In his last four games, he has had more than 15 fantasy points in any game. That could easily change this week. Among 34 qualifying passers, Darnold is 15th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 13th in highly accurate throw rate, and fourth in catchable target rate. Darnold is a strong streamer this week. He could easily post a QB1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, Chicago has allowed the most yards per attempt, the seventh-highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-highest passer rating.

Geno Smith is a solid streaming option at quarterback this week. Smith is the QB24 in fantasy points per game with two games of at least 24 fantasy points this season. He could add a third game to that ledger this week. Among 34 qualifying passers, Smith has been playing well, ranking ninth in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, second in catchable target rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the eighth-most yards per attempt, the second-highest passing success rate, the highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-most EPA per dropback.

Last week, Baker Mayfield posted only 6.7 fantasy points (QB26) in his return to the huddle. Mayfield's thumb obviously isn't 100%. He threw the ball only 11 times for 64 passing yards (5.8 yards per attempt) and a passing score. With those 11 passing attempts, Mayfield had an aDOT of 4.67 (third-lowest) and a 2.49 average time to throw (seventh-lowest). Despite the short area passing approach, Mayfield had only 36.4% of his throws deemed as highly accurate. With Tampa Bay protecting Mayfield with limited passing volume, it's impossible to feel good about plugging him into a fantasy lineup. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 14th-lowest EPA per dropback. During that span, the Falcons also have the 13th-best pressure rate and the ninth-best quick pressure rate. I expect another down week for Mayfield.

Aaron Rodgers is the QB19 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 22 fantasy points. He had a letdown game against the Saints that I didn't see coming. Among 34 qualifying passers, Rodgers is 24th in yards per attempt, 13th in passing touchdown rate, 24th in passing success rate, 19th in highly accurate throw rate, and 25th in hero throw rate. Rodgers is a low-end QB2 this week with a bad matchup. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the fifth-lowest passing success rate, and the 11th-lowest EPA per dropback.

Michael Penix is the QB18 in fantasy points per game after ripping off back-to-back QB1 outings (QB5, QB8). Among 34 qualifying passers, Penix is seventh in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 17th in catchable target rate, and 16th in hero throw rate. He has played far better than I anticipated this season. Penix could log another QB1 outing this week, but it's better to view him as a mid-range QB2. Tampa Bay's pass defense has been rounding into form. Across their last five games, they have allowed the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, the second-lowest EPA per dropback, and the 13th-lowest passing touchdown rate.

Malik Willis has had 20.9 and 26 fantasy points over his last two games, as he has started to flash the fantasy upside I forecasted in the summer. Willis had a rushing score in each game while averaging eight carries and 55.5 rushing yards. Since Week 5, among 33 qualifying passers, Willis has ranked 14th in yards per attempt, sixth in passing success rate, 30th in catchable target rate, and third in fantasy points per dropback. Willis could post another QB1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the fifth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, and the eighth-highest passing success rate.

Last week, Bo Nix flashed a fantasy pulse as the QB3 for the week. Much of that fantasy output was based on his seven carries and 73 yards (one score) on the ground, not his passing prowess. For a quarterback that, outside of last week's game, hasn't had more than ten rushing yards in any game, I don't think we can count on the rushing floor and upside weekly. Nix finished with 222 yards through the air with one touchdown, a 51.7% completion percentage, and 7.7 yards per attempt. Among 34 qualifying passers, Nix is 31st in yards per attempt, 33rd in passing success rate, 27th in passing touchdown rate, and 24th in highly accurate throw rate. I expect Nix to come back to Earth this week as a middling QB2. In their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 14th-lowest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-lowest passing success rate.

Deshaun Watson is the QB22 in fantasy points per game with two QB1 weekly finishes on the ledger for 2026 (QB10, QB11). Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 18th in yards per attempt, 26th in passing touchdown rate, 17th in passing success rate, 15th in highly accurate throw rate, and 21st in hero throw rate. He has averaged 6.9 rushing attempts and 30.7 yards on the ground with one rushing score. He's a middling QB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 11th-fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the eighth-lowest CPOE.

Justin Herbert has been a fantasy dud all year as the QB27 in fantasy points per game. He hasn't had more than 14.3 fantasy points in any game this season. Among 34 qualifying passers, Herbert has the ninth-lowest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate (tied with Baker Mayfield), and the third-fewest fantasy points per dropback (tied with Jalon Daniels). I don't really care what the matchup is right now for Herbert. He has been commanding a broken offense. I need to see him actually post a decent stat line before I'd plug him into a fantasy lineup. Sit him again this week.

Over the last two games, Tanner McKee has been the QB21 and QB22 in fantasy points per game. Among 40 qualifying passers, he is bottom of the barrel, ranking 39th in yards per attempt, passing success rate, and catchable target rate. Despite a promising matchup this week, McKee couldn't take advantage of a struggling Dallas secondary last week, so I have zero faith that he'll be able to do much against Washington this week. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the tenth-highest passing success rate, and the sixth-highest passer rating.

Daniel Jones has been a disaster this season. He doesn't have a single game with at least 275 passing yards or multiple passing touchdowns this season. Jones has one game with more than 15 rushing yards. I'm not surprised by the lack of ground game from Jones coming off the Achilles, but the fact that he is a statue who also can't throw the ball is a problem. Among 34 qualifying passers, Jones has the fourth-fewest yards per attempt, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, the fourth-lowest catchable target rate, and the fifth-highest off-target rate. Jones has finished higher than QB22 in weekly scoring only once this season (QB16 last week). Jones could have a decent yardage outing, but I don't see him stacking multiple touchdowns this week. Across their last five games, Jacksonville has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest CPOE, and ranked 17th in passing success rate, but they have held passers to the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate. Jones is a low-end QB2 again this week.

Cam Ward still barely has a pulse for fantasy as the QB36 in fantasy points per game. He has failed to eclipse 12 fantasy points in five games this season. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 33rd in yards per attempt, 28th in passing success rate, and 33rd in passing touchdown rate and fantasy points per dropback. Until any of this changes, I'm not starting Ward in any format. He's still live to get benched in any game until this level of play changes.

Last week, in his first game back, Josh Jacobs was the RB7 in fantasy scoring. He played 53.8% of the snaps with 57.9% of the rushing workload, a 43.5% route share, and a 15.6% target share. Jacobs had an 11.1% explosive run rate, 1.45 yards after contact per attempt, and a 9% missed tackle rate. Those aren't amazing numbers (outside of the explosive run rate), but it's a one-game sample, so I'm not freaking out. Jacobs finished with 16 touches and 91 total yards. It was a more substantial workload than I thought he'd get in his first game back, but five of those touches were receptions. His 11 carries were about what I thought he would see. Jacobs should have another strong game this week. Since Week 3, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt.

Chase Brown has had such a poor run out this season as the RB20 in fantasy points per game. He has one touchdown this season and is the RB12 in expected fantasy points per game. Overall, he has averaged 18.4 touches and 71.3 total yards. He has been splitting the early-down work with Samaje Perine over the last two games, while last week his snap rate jumped back to 74.5% as he also had a 59.4% route share (16.7% target share). Over the last two games, he has had a 55% rushing share while splitting the red zone work with Perine evenly (both backs have two red zone rushing attempts). This is despite Brown having a 70% snap share during that span inside the 20-yard line. Among 42 qualifying backs, Brown is 25th in yards after contact per attempt and 32nd in missed tackle rate, but his offensive line has done him no favors as he is also 33rd in yards before contact per attempt. This could be the "get right" game for Brown. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt.

Bucky Irving is the RB15 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.7 touches and 90.8 total yards. He has a 63.8% snap rate, 57.1% of the rushing work, a 47.6% route share, and a 10.7% target share. Among 42 qualifying backs, Irving is 30th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Irving should have another strong stat line this week. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the ninth-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest gap rushing success rate (Irving: 53.3% gap).

D'Andre Swift is the RB12 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.7 touches and 89.7 total yards. Swift has had a 60.4% snap rate, 47.2% of the rushing work, a 38.8% route share, and a 10.4% target share. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Swift is 19th in yards after contact per attempt and seventh in missed tackle rate. He'll have to lean on his volume and touchdown equity this week against an elite Seattle run defense. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Rhamondre Stevenson is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 13.9 touches and 69.8 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 16th in missed tackle rate and 24th in yards after contact per attempt. Stevenson is a strong RB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt, the seventh-highest gap yards per carry, and the sixth-highest gap rushing success rate (Stevenson: 68.8% gap).

Tony Pollard was a fantasy point scoring behemoth last week as the RB1 overall in fantasy. Pollard finished with 28 touches, 155 total yards, and three scores. It was an insane performance. Since Week 2, Pollard has averaged 19.2 touches and 82.3 total yards. Over the last two games, his playing time has increased with a 74.8% snap rate, 83% of the rushing workload, and a 37.5% route share (5.7% target share). Pollard has been running strong this season. Among 42 qualifying backs, Pollard is 16th in explosive run rate and tenth in yards after contact per attempt. He could have another nice stat line this week. Across their last five games, Cincy has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the fourth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt. Pollard is an RB2 with upside.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB12 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.3 touches and 97 total yards. Gordon has been outstanding. I didn't see this coming, but I'm so happy to see him excelling. Among 42 qualifying backs, Gordon is fourth in explosive run rate, 15th in yards after contact per attempt, and 18th in missed tackle rate. Gordon should have another strong showing this week. In their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.
Breece Hall opened this week (quad) with a limited practice. I'll update his outlook on Friday. He could be back this week.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB19 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.2 touches and 71.1 total yards. He has a 59.2% snap rate, 58.1% of the rushing work, and a 30.3% route share (11.4% target share). His per-touch efficiency has been horrible with only 1.80 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Judkins will need a touchdown and all the volume he can handle this week to produce a nice stat line for fantasy purposes. Over the last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-lowest explosive run rate, the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, and the fifth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

In his first start before the bye week, Rachaad White finished with 11 touches and 57 total yards as the RB10 for the week. White played 70.5% of the snaps with 41.2% of the rushing work and a 51.1% route share (12.5% target share). I expect White to see a similar workload this week. White is a volume play only. His per-touch efficiency has been decent with 2.06 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. White should have a decent outing. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the tenth-highest rushing success rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fifth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate.
I'll update Jordan Mason's outlook on Friday. Aaron Jones sustained a knee injury last week. The team has discussed him being "day-to-day", so we need to see how his practice reports look this week.

Since Week 5, Blake Corum has been the RB9 in fantasy points per game. Over the last three weeks, Corum has had a 32.7% snap rate, 38.3% of the rushing attempts, and a 12.4% route share (6% target share). During this stretch, Corum has averaged 12.3 touches and 77.6 total yards with three scores. Corum has been electric on a per-touch basis. Among 42 qualifying backs, Corum is ninth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. He should run wild again this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest gap yards per carry (Corum: 54.7% gap).
Jeremiyah Love opened this week with a limited practice (ankle). I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Braelon Allen opened this week with a limited practice (ankle). He could be the lead back again this week, but Breece Hall also opened the week with a limited practice. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Last week, Rico Dowdle was the RB22, finishing with 15 touches and 86 total yards. Dowdle played 44.4% of the snaps with 30% of the rushing attempts and a 55.9% route share (20% target share). Dowdle has a decent 2.06 yards after contact per attempt and a 10% missed tackle rate. Dowdle could post another strong week against the Browns' porous run defense. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, as Sean Payton talked about having Jonah Coleman on a snap count in his return, Coleman led the backfield in snaps (50%), rushing attempts (nine, 34.6%), and was second in route share (21.9%), running one less route than RJ Harvey. Coleman finished with 11 touches and 69 total yards. This season, with his 19 carries, he has a wonderful 23.5% explosive run rate and 52.6% success rate, while his 1.69 yards after contact per attempt and 11% missed tackle rate aren't anything to write home about. Coleman is a low-end flex this week because his role is still in flux and the matchup is horrible. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Emanuel Wilson bounced back as the RB8 for the week. Wilson could easily lead the backfield again in touches this week, but we have to wait on Zach Charbonnet news. I'll update his outlook on Saturday.

Last week, RJ Harvey had a big play in the passing game and a touchdown that helped save his day, but his usage was concerning. With Jonah Coleman back. Harvey had only a 25% snap rate, three rushing attempts (11.5% of the rushing work), and a 25% route share (6.9% target share). Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the tenth-most yards per target to backs, so it's a good matchup for Harvey in his passing game role. I can't plug him into a flex spot this week, though. His workload could evaporate this week in a blink if Jonah Coleman's role grows more. If Harvey didn't have the one big play and score last week, it wouldn't be a question at all. He'd be a locked-in sit this week.

Mike McDaniel has capsized Omarion Hampton as the RB31 in fantasy points per game. Hampton has averaged 14.8 touches and 57.5 total yards. In the Bolts dumpster fire backfield, Hampton has had a 45.6% snap rate, 47.3% of the rushing work, and a 22.6% route share (5% target share). Among 42 qualifying backs, Hampton is ninth in yards after contact per attempt and 28th in missed tackle rate. Hampton is just a touchdown-dependent flex again this week. The Rams have slowly tightened up their run defense to league average standards. Over their last five games, they have been 15th in explosive run rate, 14th in rushing success rate, and have allowed the 12th-lowest missed tackle rate.
Saquon Barkley sustained a back injury last week. He opened this week with a DNP. I'll update his outlook on Friday. He could easily miss this week.
Aaron Jones sustained a knee injury last week. He opened this week with a DNP. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

I'll dive into Tyler Allegier's outlook on Friday. It'll depend upon Jeremiyah Love's possible return this week. Love opened this week with a limited practice (ankle). Allgeier also opened this week with a DNP (toe), so there's plenty of uncertainty swirling around this backfield for Week 8.

Samaje Perine is a viable flex this week. Over the last two games, Perine has split the red zone work evenly with Chase Brown (two rushing attempts each) while averaging ten touches and 47 total yards. Perine has mustered a decent 10.3% explosive run rate and 2.29 yards after contact per attempt this season. Tennessee has fielded a putrid run defense recently. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt. If Perine scores a touchdown with 10-12 touches this week, he could easily be a nice flex play.

Since Week 6, TreVeyon Henderson has continued to operate as Rhamondre Stevenson's change of pace with a 23.8% snap rate, 6.5 touches, and 31.5 total yards per game. Henderson is only a dart-throw flex with a good matchup. Henderson's rushing efficiency continues to be non-existent with only 1.79 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate, but we know his home run speed is real. If he gets a crease, he can take any carry to the house. If you're flexing him this week, this is exactly what you're hoping for. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt, the seventh-highest gap yards per carry, and the sixth-highest gap rushing success rate (Henderson: 65.4% gap).

Last week, J.K. Dobbins' role shrank as he finished with only six rushing attempts, 23 yards on the ground, and a touchdown. It was his lowest rushing attempt mark of the season while also having a season-low 23% snap rate. The Denver backfield seems to be shifting more in the direction of Jonah Coleman, which makes Dobbins a worrisome flex with a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate. Sit Dobbins.

Tetairoa McMillan is the WR13 in fantasy points per game. In the four games he has played with Jalen Coker as a full-time player, McMillan has had a 21.5% target share with 2.19 YPRR, four red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 27.9% first-read share. This week McMillan faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four games with Coker as a full-go, McMillan has had a 21% TPRR and 2.67 YPRR against two high. McMillan has a nice shot at a bounce-back game this week against a Green Bay secondary that (since Week 3) has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

George Pickens is the WR24 in fantasy points per game with at least 15 PPR points in two of his last three games. I'm projecting a milder stat line this week for Pickens. Yes, you guessed it. Arizona is a two-high, heavy pass defense. Pickens has a 20.5% target share with 2.00 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 23.1% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Against two high, Pickens' TPRR drops off a map from 35% (against single high) to 17%, and his YPRR falls from 2.92 to 1.51. Working in his favor is the fact that Arizona has been horrible at defending perimeter wide receivers, which could help counteract Pickens' coverage woes. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Pickens could still be a decent WR2 this week, but this doesn't look like a blow-up spot.

Jalen Coker didn't have the massive game last week that I was projecting, as Carolina's passing offense cratered as Bryce Young fell back to Earth. Coker could have a bounce-back outing this week. In his four full games this season, Coker has had a 22.2% target share with 2.40 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 30.2% first-read share. Overall, he is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. This week, Coker faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four full games, against two-high, Coker has had a 23% TPRR with 1.85 YPRR. Bryce Young will have to look like his early-season form for this passing attack to have bite again, but it's possible. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

Garrett Wilson is the WR22 in fantasy points per game, but he has had fewer than nine PPR points in three of his last four games. With that said, Wilson could get the squeaky wheel treatment this week. Overall, Wilson still has a 25.1% target share with 2.09 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 30.6% first-read share. His quiet Week 6 performance is easily explainable, as he had to deal with Christian Gonzalez on 93.9% of his routes. The Raiders don't have a corner in that talent area code on their depth chart. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fifth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Michael Wilson has been struggling recently. Wilson is still the WR32 in fantasy points per game, but he hasn't managed more than 12 PPR points since Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure from Arizona. Since Week 5, he has had a 16% target share with 1.01 YPRR, three red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 17.8% first-read share. He hasn't finished with more than 55 receiving yards in any of these three games. Hopefully, he breaks out of the funk this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. There's a wide range of outcomes for Wilson this week, which makes him difficult to trust as anything more than a flex with upside.

Ok, let's start this off with A.J. Brown isn't fully healthy. I don't care what New England says. Brown doesn't pass the eye test.
